fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled attribute value from the XML input (attr="\u00e9", UTF-8 bytes 0xC3 0xA9) is stored as a text child of the attribute node, so the non-ASCII bytes enter the tree as attr->children->content.

DTD validation (xmlCtxtValidateDocument -> xmlValidateDocumentInternal -> xmlValidateElement) fetches the attribute's text children; inLine=0 sets escape=1 and flags=XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII|XML_ESCAPE_ATTR (doc->encoding is NULL, list->parent is an attribute node).
The text node content containing the non-ASCII byte 0xC3 is passed to xmlEscapeText together with the XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII flag, which selects the hex char-ref escaping branch.
The inner scan loop stops at the first non-ASCII byte (c=0xC3 >= 0x80) with offset still -1, so control falls into the else branch that builds the replacement string in a stack buffer.
tempBuf is declared inside the else block; its lifetime ends at the closing brace of that block while repl still points into it, which is the stack-use-after-scope root cause.
The hex char ref "é" (6 bytes) is written into tempBuf and repl is set to point at the stack buffer whose scope is about to end.
memcpy reads replSize (6) bytes from repl, which points into the expired tempBuf stack object; ASan reports stack-use-after-scope at this memcpy.

issue_alignment.admission: valid fuzz target reads 4-byte opts and 4-byte failurePos, then a backslash-newline-terminated URL/entity string pair; the entity is parsed with XML_PARSE_DTDVALID and post-validated with xmlCtxtValidateDocument
issue_alignment.source: non-ASCII UTF-8 attribute value in crafted XML is stored as attribute text child by xmlSAX2AttributeNs
issue_alignment.root_cause: xmlEscapeText declares tempBuf inside the else block and lets repl outlive its scope
issue_alignment.propagation: attr children -> xmlNodeListGetString -> xmlNodeListGetStringInternal -> xmlEscapeText with XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII flag
issue_alignment.sink: memcpy(out, repl, replSize) reads stale stack memory after tempBuf lifetime ended
